item.description: The label will appear on the player page and include songs entirely generated by AI or partially, such as AI involved in composition and vocals.

item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

item.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
item.description: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

item.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

item.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
item.description: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

item.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
item.description: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

item.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
item.description: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

item.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
item.description: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

item.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
item.description: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

item.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
item.description: Google is making it easier to build and use personal Android apps created with AI, without having to make them available to everyone on the Play Store.
